Body: Style suggestion: Imports should be grouped at the top of the file with the other imports, not placed mid-file after the `getCurrentProject` function.

The Modal loader should include the apiKey in the returned options when it's available. While the SDK will automatically use provider.key from Auth (line 1173), it's more explicit and consistent with other OpenAI-compatible providers (like GitLab at line 564) to include the apiKey directly in the options. This ensures the provider works correctly when the API key is configured via environment variables or config file, not just via Auth.
```suggestion
          baseURL,
          ...(apiKey ? { apiKey } : {}),
```

The Modal provider model definition is duplicated between the routes file (lines 44-73) and the provider.ts file (lines 873-908). This creates a maintenance burden as any changes to model capabilities, limits, or URLs need to be updated in both places. Consider extracting the Modal provider definition to a shared constant or using the database definition from provider.ts in the routes file.

The Modal provider integration includes custom model discovery logic that dynamically fetches available models from the API endpoint. This behavior should be covered by tests to ensure it works correctly in scenarios like: API key is available and model discovery succeeds, API key is missing and fallback model is used, API returns an error and fallback model is used, and API timeout is handled properly. Consider adding tests similar to those in packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts for other providers.

The JSON.parse call could throw if opts.body is not valid JSON. While this is unlikely in practice (since the SDK should generate valid JSON), consider wrapping this in a try-catch block to prevent the entire fetch from failing if the body is malformed. This would make the code more defensive against unexpected SDK behavior.

The reasoning content is being placed at the beginning of the content array, which changes the original order of parts. If the original message had reasoning parts interspersed with text or tool parts, this transformation will move all reasoning to the front. While this may be intentional for the Anthropic SDK's expectations, consider whether preserving the original order is important for maintaining context. If order matters, the reasoning part should be inserted at the position of the first reasoning part found.

There are no tests covering the new Anthropic SDK code path for non-Claude models with interleaved reasoning. Consider adding test cases that verify: 1) reasoning parts are converted to thinking blocks with the placeholder signature for Anthropic SDK models with interleaved field, 2) the fetch wrapper correctly transforms thinking blocks back to reasoning_content field, 3) edge cases like empty reasoning text or multiple reasoning parts are handled correctly.
```suggestion
            ],
            providerOptions: msg.providerOptions,
```

The use of a placeholder signature "interleaved-placeholder" relies on internal SDK behavior to force the Anthropic SDK to serialize reasoning parts as thinking blocks. This approach is fragile because: 1) it depends on undocumented SDK behavior that could change, 2) the SDK might validate or reject the placeholder value, 3) future SDK versions might handle this differently. Consider adding a comment documenting this dependency and the risk, or exploring if there's an official SDK API to control this serialization.

The `continue` statement on line 958 will skip all remaining plugins in the outer loop, not just the github-copilot-enterprise processing. This means if `github-copilot-enterprise` has an explicit API key configured, no subsequent plugins will be processed at all. This should likely be a nested conditional structure or the enterprise processing should be refactored into a separate block to avoid this issue.

The model format example uses `openai/gpt-5`, but GPT-5 has not been released yet (as of February 2026). This could confuse users who might think this is a real model they can use. Consider using an existing model like `openai/gpt-4` or `openai/gpt-4-turbo` instead to avoid confusion.
```suggestion
- `model` must be a string like `openai/gpt-4-turbo`, not an object
```

The condition `if (str)` will evaluate to false for empty strings, which are valid inputs for the match function. This could cause incorrect behavior when comparing empty strings. Consider using `if (str !== undefined && str !== null)` or a more explicit check instead.

This test appears to be checking path normalization, but the first argument to `Wildcard.match` contains a literal asterisk at the end. After normalization, both arguments become `"C:/Windows/System32/*"`, and the pattern's asterisk will be converted to a wildcard regex `.*`. This means the test is actually checking if a literal asterisk in the string matches a wildcard pattern, which may not be the intended behavior for a test named "match normalizes slashes for cross-platform globbing". Consider using a concrete path like `"C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers"` for the first argument to better test slash normalization without the ambiguity of the literal asterisk.
```suggestion
  expect(Wildcard.match("C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers", "C:/Windows/System32/*")).toBe(true)
```

The test creates a file at line 202 (tmpfile) but the command at line 206 attempts to remove a directory (nested). This inconsistency suggests that either the file creation or the rm command is incorrect. If the test is meant to verify that rm doesn't trigger external_directory permission for internal paths, consider either removing the file creation line or changing the rm command to target the created file.
```suggestion
            command: `rm -rf ${path.join(tmp.path, "tmpfile")}`,
            description: "remove tmp file",
```

The generated SDK method signature has text as optional (text?: string), but the actual API validation requires text to be present (z.string().trim().min(1) in session.ts). The SessionSteerData type should have body be required, not optional. This discrepancy means TypeScript won't catch if the caller forgets to provide the text parameter. Consider updating the OpenAPI schema or generated types to make body required.
```suggestion
  body: {
```

The `text` parameter in the steer method is typed as optional (`text?: string`) but the server route validates it as required with `.trim().min(1)`. This mismatch between client SDK and server validation could lead to runtime errors. The parameter should either be marked as required in the SDK types or the server validation should handle the optional case.
```suggestion
      text: string
```

If `writeSteer` throws an error (e.g., "No user message found to attach steer metadata"), the steer item will still be pushed to `match.steerQueue` (line 308), but the steer message won't be persisted to the database. This could lead to inconsistent state where the queue indicates a steer message exists but it's not in storage. Consider adding error handling to either rollback the queue update or retry the write operation.

The E2E test uses a non-existent model identifier "openai/gpt-5.2". While this works because the test uses `noReply: true` and never actually invokes the model, it could be confusing for future test authors. Consider using a clearly fake model name like "test/fake-model" or a comment explaining why a non-existent model is acceptable here.
```suggestion
            model: "test/fake-model",
```

The `drainSteerQueue` function empties the steer queue using `splice(0)` but doesn't utilize the queued items. While the steer messages are already persisted to the database via `writeSteer`, the queue contains timestamp information that could be useful for ordering. Currently, there's no guarantee that steer messages will be processed in timestamp order if multiple steer calls happen rapidly. Consider sorting the queue by timestamp before draining, or document why timestamp ordering is not necessary.

The `text` parameter is marked as optional in the TypeScript signature (`text?: string`) but the server-side validation requires it to be a non-empty string (`z.string().trim().min(1)`). This inconsistency could lead to runtime validation errors when calling the API without providing the text parameter. The SDK should mark this parameter as required to match the server validation: change `text?: string` to `text: string`.
```suggestion
      text: string
```

`SessionCompaction.lastPrompt` currently treats `TextPart.ignored` content as eligible for the preserved prompt. But ignored text parts are intentionally excluded from `MessageV2.toModelMessages`, so including them here can leak user-only/ignored content into the post-compaction context and may select the wrong “last prompt”. Consider filtering with the same criteria as `toModelMessages` (e.g., require `p.type === "text" && !p.synthetic && !p.ignored`) both in the `findLast` predicate and the `filter`/`map` pipeline.
```suggestion
    const match = msgs.findLast(
      (m) =>
        m.info.role === "user" &&
        m.parts.some((p) => p.type === "text" && !p.synthetic && !p.ignored),
    )
    if (!match) return undefined
    const text = match.parts
      .filter((p): p is MessageV2.TextPart => p.type === "text" && !p.synthetic && !p.ignored)
```

`state.sqlite` is assigned immediately after creating the BunDatabase, but `Client` initialization can still throw later (e.g., during migrations). If an error is thrown, `lazy()` will retry on the next call and `state.sqlite` may get overwritten, leaking the original open handle and making `close()` behavior ambiguous. Consider only setting `state.sqlite` after successful initialization, or ensuring the created handle is closed/cleared on initialization failure.

Inconsistency with production code: The test passes `tmp.path + "/"` to `createRequire`, but the production code in config.ts line 1340 passes `options.path` (the full path to opencode.json file). For consistency and to accurately test the production behavior, this should be `createRequire(path.join(tmp.path, "opencode.json"))`. Additionally, using string concatenation with "/" could cause issues on Windows where paths use backslashes.
```suggestion
        const require = createRequire(path.join(tmp.path, "opencode.json"))
```

The test expects patterns to be normalized with forward slashes, but reviewing bash.ts (lines 145-148), the bash tool doesn't appear to normalize glob patterns before adding them to ctx.ask when the directory doesn't start with "/". On Windows, os.tmpdir() returns something like "C:\Users\...\Temp", which path.join would convert to "C:\Users\...\Temp\*" with backslashes. Consider verifying that the bash tool normalizes patterns consistently with assertExternalDirectory (external-directory.ts:21 uses `.replaceAll("\\", "/")`), or if normalization happens elsewhere in the request pipeline, consider adding a code comment explaining this behavior for future maintainers.

`page.keyboard.press("Control+A")` is not cross-platform and deviates from the existing E2E convention of using `modKey` for shortcuts (see `packages/app/e2e/utils.ts:10` and e.g. `${modKey}+A` in `packages/app/e2e/session/session-undo-redo.spec.ts`). Please switch this to `${modKey}+A` (or Playwright’s `ControlOrMeta+A`) and import `modKey` to keep the test runnable on macOS as well.

The PR description mentions that Cygwin paths like "/c/Users/..." or "C:/Users/..." should match against native roots like "C:\Users\...", but there are no test cases verifying this behavior. Consider adding test cases to ensure Cygwin path compatibility works as intended, for example testing paths starting with "/c/" or "/cygdrive/c/" against a Windows root.
```suggestion
    expect(path.normalize("c:\\repo\\src\\app.ts")).toBe("src\\app.ts")
    // Cygwin-style paths should also normalize against the Windows root
    expect(path.normalize("/c/repo/src/app.ts")).toBe("src/app.ts")
    expect(path.normalize("/cygdrive/c/repo/src/app.ts")).toBe("src/app.ts")
```

The canonicalization always lowercases both the root and path, even on non-Windows systems. This could cause issues on case-sensitive filesystems (Linux/Mac) where "/repo/Src/app.ts" and "/repo/src/app.ts" are different files. The original code only applied case-insensitive matching on Windows (when root started with a drive letter). Consider adding back the Windows detection to only lowercase on Windows systems.

The CI check for disabling Bun cache is added here to fix Windows e2e flakiness, but there's another Bun install operation in `packages/opencode/src/bun/index.ts:96` that also uses `--no-cache` with `proxied()` but doesn't check for `process.env.CI`. If the Bun cache ENOENT issue affects this location, it might also affect the other install operation. Consider whether the CI check should be applied consistently to both locations, or document why this fix is only needed for config/plugin dependency installs.

The magic number 0x08000000 should be replaced with a named constant for better maintainability. In cli.rs, the codebase imports CREATE_NO_WINDOW from windows::Win32::System::Threading. Consider importing and using this constant here as well, or defining a module-level constant with a descriptive name.

The extract_exe function has a potential logic issue. When a quoted path is found (line 216-222), it only returns if the path contains ".exe". However, if a quoted path doesn't contain ".exe", it falls through to line 225 which searches for ".exe" in the original value string, potentially extracting from both inside and outside the quotes. This could lead to incorrect behavior when processing registry values or command files with mixed quoted and unquoted content. Consider returning None for quoted paths that don't contain ".exe" instead of falling through to the unquoted logic.

The resolve_windows_app_path function may have significant performance implications. It makes multiple sequential system calls (where, reg query multiple times) without any caching mechanism. For the registry queries alone, it checks 3 different registry keys per executable candidate, and with multiple candidates being generated, this could result in dozens of subprocess spawns. Consider adding a caching layer (e.g., using once_cell or lazy_static with a Mutex-protected HashMap) to cache resolved paths, especially since app locations rarely change during runtime.

The new resolve_windows_app_path function and its helper functions (expand_env, extract_exe, candidates, reg_app_path) lack unit tests. Given the complexity of this logic with multiple edge cases (quoted paths, environment variable expansion, registry parsing, path normalization), this code would benefit from comprehensive unit tests similar to the test coverage seen in linux_windowing.rs. Consider adding tests for scenarios like: paths with spaces, quoted vs unquoted paths, environment variable expansion, registry value parsing, and the various candidate generation strategies.

The magic number 0x08000000 should be replaced with a named constant for better maintainability. In cli.rs, the codebase imports CREATE_NO_WINDOW from windows::Win32::System::Threading. Consider importing and using this constant here as well, or defining a module-level constant with a descriptive name.

The contract assertion collects parameter names without checking `in === "query"`. If the OpenAPI generator later adds header/path parameters to `/event`, this test will start failing (or pass for the wrong reason). Filtering to only `parameters` entries where `in` is `"query"` would better match the test intent and make it less brittle.
```suggestion
    const names = params
      .flatMap((item) =>
        "name" in item &&
        typeof item.name === "string" &&
        "in" in item &&
        item.in === "query"
          ? [item.name]
          : [],
      )
      .sort()
```

These `/event` requests will run through `Server`'s `Instance.provide({ init: InstanceBootstrap, ... })` middleware. Because this test doesn’t pre-seed the `Instance` cache, the first request will trigger `InstanceBootstrap()` (LSP init, file watcher init, etc.), which can add significant overhead and leave background resources running during the test suite. Consider wrapping the request(s) in `await Instance.provide({ directory: process.cwd(), fn: async () => ... })` (or passing an explicit `directory` query/header and pre-providing the same directory) so the server middleware reuses the cached instance and skips bootstrap.

The macOS ignore list is built with a long sequence of `ignore.add(...)` calls, which is a bit error-prone to maintain (easy to miss/duplicate entries). Consider defining the list as an array (or constant) and adding via a simple loop so it’s easier to audit and update.
```suggestion
          const macOsIgnore = [
            "Applications",
            "Desktop",
            "Documents",
            "Downloads",
            "Library",
            "Movies",
            "Music",
            "Pictures",
            "Public",
          ]
          for (const name of macOsIgnore) {
            ignore.add(name)
          }
```

This change alters the directory discovery behavior for the global home case on macOS (skipping common user folders to avoid permission prompts), but there doesn’t appear to be test coverage for this path. Consider adding a unit test that asserts these folder names are excluded when `isGlobalHome` on darwin (potentially by factoring the ignore-list construction into a helper that can be tested without having to mutate `process.platform`).

The regex uses a single backslash `\s` instead of double backslash `\\s`, which will be interpreted as an invalid escape sequence in a string literal. This should be `/\s+/` (no string escaping needed in regex literal) or if this is meant to be a string pattern, it needs proper escaping.

The onDragEnd handler doesn't release pointer capture. When pointer capture is set via setPointerCapture at line 28, it should be released in onDragEnd using releasePointerCapture. The same issue exists in onResizeEnd. Without releasing capture, the pointer may remain captured even after dragging/resizing ends.

The event listeners are created but never unsubscribed after the promptAsync call completes. If multiple submissions happen or if the component unmounts, these listeners will leak. The unsub() and unsub2() calls on lines 72-73 only execute in the success path. They should be moved to a finally block or the error path should also clean them up.

The Playground components use hardcoded English strings instead of using the i18n system. The PR adds translations to en.ts but they're never used. Components should use language.t() to reference the translation keys for consistency with the rest of the codebase and to support future internationalization.

The canvasRect prop is passed to PlaygroundWindowComponent but never used. This appears to be dead code. Either implement the functionality that was intended to use this prop (likely for constraining window bounds to canvas) or remove the unused prop.
